Commentary.Commentary: Yet another pink-ball Test match has yielded result. The cricketing world is yet to see a drawn day-night Test. England were thoroughly outplayed in this one by the Kiwis. But they need not be dejected. They have another chance to make a comeback in the series. The second Test begins on 30th March, 2018 at 1100 local (2200 GMT, the previous day). See ya then! Ta-ta! Take care, aficionados!

Kane Williamson, the victorious Kiwi skipper, is happy with the win and credits the first innings efforts with the ball for the same. Adds that they did well to face the opposition bowling which is full of quality. States that they always look to execute their plans and feel good that they came off in this game. Feels proud about the partnerships in this innings. Mentions about England's bowling being good which reflects in the slow pace of their stands. Opines that their plan in the game was to always focus on the present and not to look far too ahead. About Todd Astle, he says that the bowling was good from him. Adds that he had to bide his time and came good when he was summoned. Agrees that it is tough to snatch the ball away from an energetic cricketer like Neil Wagner. Ends looking forward to keeping up this good work in the following Test.

Joe Root, the English skipper, says that this was a bad game for them. Admits to it being difficult to get back in the game after a poor start like they had. States that they couldn't generate much swing with the ball. Says that the fight that they showed today was something he wishes to see more. Reckons that his finger is good and he should be fit for the next Test. Ends saying that he needs to improve on his own game going forward.

Trent Boult is the Man of the Match for his 9-99 in this game. He reckons that the way they achieved the win was terrific. States the importance of picking up 20 wickets in a Test match. Opines that today they needed some hard work to skittle out the opposition. Mentions about the night session being the best one for the bowlers in the day-night Tests.

For the home side, Trent Boult, Neil Wagner and Todd Astle picked up 3 wickets each, with Tim Southee picking one. The way Wagner was charging in on this final day would have made any pacer proud. The venom in his spell just HAD TO translate into wickets and rightly so, he was the one with the decisive wickets of Stokes and Woakes in this innings. Presentation follows in a bit...

The final day began with an early wicket (Dawid Malan). But then, Ben Stokes spent some time in the middle along with Jonny Bairstow and Moeen Ali. The English keeper couldn't make use of a couple of lives to string a big one. Stokes then stuck in their with Chris Woakes for 83 runs. Although both of them got past their half centuries, it wasn't enough to avert an innings defeat.

With a mountain of runs in front, the English batters, basically had to see off some four and a half sessions to salvage a draw. Often, the game tests you psychologically. Although Alastair Cook departed soon, Mark Stoneman and Joe Root kept them in the game with an 88-run stand. But then both of them departed. The skipper fell on what turned out to be the last delivery of the penultimate day to swing the balance decisively in the hosts' favour.

About Test matches, it is often said that if you bat once and bat big, often you are in a safe position. New Zealand did just that. First Kane Williamson and then Henry Nicholls struck magnificent tons to deflate the English bowlers. Although they didn't have any triple-figure stand, the contributions of the duo apart from some more useful ones helped them post a big score. For the tourists, James Anderson and Stuart Broad picked up three apiece but couldn't do much to prevent a 369-run lead.

The seeds of this terrific win was sown on the first day when Trent Boult and Tim Southee combined to bowl England out for 58. The left-arm pacer's six-fer absolutely destroyed the visitors. In helpful conditions after winning the toss, the Kiwis didn't have to look for any other option than the two seamers. The final wicket stand of 31 runs for England helped them at least cross the 50-run mark.

Neil Wagner is caught up on the sidelines by Simon Doull. He states that his side stuck it out to end up victorious in this game. He reckons that the practice sessions helped them and hence the result isn't a surprise. Iterates that the pink ball shaped up well and the track also assisted it. Says that they will savor this win and celebrate in the dressing room.

Clinical! That's one word to describe the Kiwis' performance. They had to pick 7 wickets coming into the last day and although nobody would have had a doubt, they set about with their task in right earnest. Yes, there was a phase when wickets weren't coming. But that's when their resolve was steely and it showed in the end result.

On the stumps, blocked solidly from the crease.
Another banged in delivery on the stumps, Overton crouched low for the keeper to collect.

Hello! Good to have you back with us for this final segment of the first day and night Test match in New Zealand. We have 32 possible overs to be bowled. Will be interesting to see if we will even need those many. Neil Wagner will continue his pending over. Craig Overton is the new batsman in.
... Final Day, Final Session ...

Stokes brought up his well-deserved fifty in the first half of this session. His presence in the middle would have raised hopes of England salvaging a draw. Kane Williamson brought on his spinner Todd Astle but with not much success. Credit should be given to the hosts as they never let their energy levels dip, even when wickets were hard to come by. New Zealand are still 69 runs ahead at the moment. Will that figure suffice them for picking the last three English wickets? Do we have some twist in the tale? See you, aficionados, in a few minutes to find out just that.

Wow! After a rather staid session, Ben Stokes' wicket at the end of it has just spiced the meal up. All through this segment, the Kiwi bowlers were toiling hard, bowling maidens after maidens, dots and dots, bouncers after bouncers to try and eke out a wicket or two. But nothing seemed to separate the duo of Stokes and Chris Woakes. Both mixed caution with aggression in building a partnership that was worth 83. In the end, all it took was persistence and discipline and Neil Wagner was rewarded for the same. This wasn't before some frustration started creeping in, in the Black Caps' camp.

OUT! Rejoice for New Zealand, Stokes' recklessness has cost him and his side a wicket! And again, at the stroke of a break. Just at the stroke of Tea this afternoon, Ali departed and here is the big English all-rounder, walking back and sort of throwing his wicket away, which eventually turns out to be the last delivery of the session. This is after the skipper Joe Root was dismissed in what turned out to be the last ball of Day 4. After living on the edge for the past 15-20 minutes, Stokes perishes in a bid to be adventurous. Gets another short length delivery outside off, he arches back and looks to upper cut it towards the vacant third man region. Doesn't make good contact and ends up hitting it in the air towards backward point. Southee runs back and takes it safely with a slide. The reaction on Wagner's face shows how much this means to him and his team. Is this the opening that seals the game? Nonetheless, Ben Stokes' innings of substance comes to an end. With that, it's the FINAL SUPPER BREAK IN THE TEST.

Gets a thick outside edge that flies over the gap between the keeper and first slip for a boundary. More frustration for the Kiwis as even the edges aren't going to the fielders.

FOUR! Flatter down leg, Woakes goes back to work it away round the corner. Seems to have missed it and the ball goes off the keeper's gloves to the fence behind. But the umpire has awarded the runs to the batter.
Beaten! Floated around off, it draws Woakes forward in defense before teasingly spinning away past the outside edge and going into the keeper's gloves. This bloke is getting the ball to turn here.

Another short length ball, pulled towards square leg. End of a 'short' maiden over, consecutive ones for the hosts.
Another short of a length ball, he tucks it down towards backward square leg for nothing. It is hard to understand the absence of a short leg fielder when the tactic is to bowl short on the body.
Wagner comes round the wicket and bangs it short. Ben stays back and defends it with a straight bat.
Another one on a length, going down leg. Stokes looks to work it away but then withdraws his blade and lets it be.

The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Full around off, Stokes looks to drive but gets an inside edge and the ball goes to the short fine leg fielder.
The TV shows us dark clouds approaching towards Eden Park. This is something New Zealand wouldn't want and maybe some England fans need.
Drags his length back and Chris blocks it well.
A tad fuller outside off, Woakes throws the kitchen sink at it but gets beaten.
Outside off, left alone.
Length in line of the stumps, Chris blocks it from within the crease.
Outside off, Woakes cuts it past the point fielder and gets a couple of runs for it.
Length on off, Woakes gives this to the mid off fielder to collect.
Stokes gets behind the ball and blocks it outside his off pole.
Straighter in line of the stumps, Ben plays this along the turf.
FOUR! A controlled pull shot from Ben. He is starting to get a move on. Another short ball, Ben rocks back and pulls this front of square for a boundary.
Defended off the front foot by Stokes presenting the full face of the bat.
Fuller in length, Ben plays this into the ground.
Stokes gets behind the ball and taps it in front of him.
Length on middle, Woakes plays it with a straight bat.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Similar length on off, Woakes pushes this in the gap through covers and comes back for the second run.
Back of a length ball, Woakes defends it by getting behind the ball.
On leg, Stokes flicks it away for one towards the square leg fielder.
FOUR! Short ball outside off, Ben waits for it and pulls it front of square for a boundary.
Comes in from round the wicket and serves this on a good length on middle and off, Woakes does not offer a shot.
Length outside off, Woakes sees it through.
Outside off, Chris shoulders arms to it.

FOUR! Lucky Woakes and a very good line from Boult. Lands this around off, the ball moves away from Chris, who thinks of driving it and then withdraws his bat at the last moment. In doing so, he ball takes the edge of the bat and flies wide past the third slip fielder for a boundary.
Full again on middle, Woakes plays it with a straight bat.
Full around off, Woakes gets it off the inner half towards mid on.
Length in line of the stumps, Ben gets behind the ball and blocks it.
Length outside off, Stokes watches it go to the keeper.
Full and wide outside off, Ben lets it be.
Length on off, Stokes punches this off his back foot to the off side.
Fuller in length, Stokes hits it to mid on for nothing.
Too wide for Stokes to play at it.
Teases Woakes by bowling it outside off, but he leaves it alone.
Welcomes Woakes with a yorker who does well to keep it at bay.
Welcome back to our coverage for this Test match. The umpires and the players have had their tea and are back in the field. Boult will continue his over while Chris Woakes is the new batsman in.
... Day 5, Session 2 ...

For the visitors now they will hope that their tail sticks along with Stokes, who has the ability to bat for long hours. If they want to save this game by any means, they will have to be more watchful. Will England get to the last session or are New Zealand going to rip through this lower order with the new ball? Stay tuned to find out.

Another wicket just before the close of a session. How unlucky are the English players? Well they were being patient and not interfering with the balls outside off but New Zealand found a way to sneak through. The day started with Dawid Malan falling pretty early. Ben Stokes and Jonny Bairstow then got along and made the hosts work for their wickets. The duo was more than happy to play the waiting game. Jonny was given a couple of lives before eventually falling to a very good catch by the Kiwi skipper. And just when Moeen Ali started to look good, he fell to Boult, in what turned out to be the last ball of the session.

OUT! New Zealand have got this review spot on! There was no inside edge on that and Ali has to depart. Boult lands this on a good length around off. The ball jags back a little and hurries onto Moeen, who tries to block it. He doesn't get behind the ball and the ball hits him on the pad. Seems to be an inside edge there on the first look and hence the umpire turns down the appeal. Williamson has a word with Boult and they decide to take it to the TV umpire. On the replays, it is seen that the ball brushed the front pad first, before taking the inside edge of the bat and going onto the back pad. The Hot Spot confirms that by showing a spot on the front pad before the ball hits the bat. The Hawk Eye shows three reds, on seeing which the crowd roars. Ali has to walk back after yet another failure. With that, Tea has been taken on the final day.
A review for LBW is been taken upstairs. Boult is smiles after the decision is gone against him. They opt for the review. Is there an inside edge?
Outside off, Ali cuts it to the gully fielder for nothing.
FOUR! Edge and a boundary! Outside off, Ali plays it with soft hands and the ball gets an edge and falls short of the second slip. It goes under him and rolls to the third man boundary.
Stokes nudges this down fine leg to move to the other end.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for the southpaw. This one is outside off, Moeen opens the face and plays it with an angled bat past gully for a boundary. The trail is now 157.
FOUR! Pitches this one up, Ali gets ahead and drives this handsomely in the gap through covers for a boundary.
On leg again, Ali works it with a wristy shot for nothing.
This ball is way wide on the leg side but Moeen still goes after it.
Teases him by bowling it outside off, Ali doesn't fall for the trap.
Comes in from round the wicket, Moeen watches this go to the keeper.
Tim Southee to run in from the other end.
Length ball outside off, Stokes is happy to let it pass by. Boult starts the second new ball with a maiden.
Outside off, left alone.
Full around off, Stokes gets low and plays it towards the off side.
Too wide to make Stokes to play at this.
Around off, Stokes hits this to mid on.
Outside off, an easy leave for Ben.
The second new ball is available and has been taken by the Kiwis. Trent Boult to have a go first with it.
In line of the stumps, Moeen is solid in defense.
Outside off again, Ali doesn't bother playing at it.
Full outside off, Ali shoulders arms to it. The keeper gets it at a good height.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Strays on the pads this time, Stokes helps it on its way for one.
Kane starts by bowling a full one around off, Stokes drives it to covers.
Kane Williamson brings himself on to bowl.
Darts this on full on middle and leg, Ali flicks it away for a dot.
Around off, spins away from Ali who plays and misses.
FOUR! Floated ball outside off, Moeen gets low and sweeps it through square leg for a boundary.
Full on the stumps, Ali whips this to mid-wicket.
Tosses this one up, Ali leans forward in defense.
Outside off, Ali lets it be.
Pulls this front of square for a run to end the over.
Another short ball on leg, Ali goes for the pull but misses it. Watling collects it and asks the umpire who shakes his head.
Short again, Ali pulls this to the short fine leg fielder for a dot.
FOUR! Another short ball which has been pulled away towards deep square leg for a boundary. Moeen is showing that he is not afraid to play the bouncers.
Digs this one short, Ali ducks under it in time.
Short ball on middle, Ali pulls this to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Short ball on off, Stokes punches this towards extra cover and gets two from it.
Darts this on the pads of Ali who flicks it away towards square leg for one.
Full outside off, Ali takes a step and gets behind the ball to play it onto the ground.
Tossed up, Ali strides forward and blocks it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tossed up, Stokes drives this through covers for a run.
FOUR! Wagner teases Ali with another bouncer on leg, Moeen pulls this with one leg up towards deep fine leg for a boundary. The fielder there dives but the ball goes past him.
Ali picked that bouncer early and lets it through to the keeper.
Wagner bangs this on short, Ali tries to sway away from it but gets hit on the chest. No damage done.
Outside off, left alone.
Back of a length ball, Ali hangs back and taps it to the off side.
Length on middle and leg, Stokes eases this through mid-wicket for a run.
Moeen shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Gives this air, Ali gets behind the ball and is solid in his defense.
Strays down the leg, Stokes helps it on its way for one more.
Flatter ball on off, Stokes defends this off his back foot.
Floated ball, Ali pushes this towards covers for one.
Serves this outside off, the ball spins in and rushes into Ali who blocks it.
Comes round the wicket, does Wagner, and bowls it on the pads. Ali nudges it through square leg for a single.
On a back of a length, Ali moves away from the line to let it be.
A low full toss on middle and leg, pushed with a straight bat to mid on.
Fuller one around off and middle, turned away to mid-wicket for a single.
This one is pushed to the off side off the back foot.
On a back of a length around off and middle, Stokes hops and blocks.
Moeen has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tosses this one on off, Ali shoulders arms to it.
Moeen Ali walks in next to bat.

OUT! Kane Williamson does not take easy catches. He absolutely flies onto this to take another great catch in this match. Short ball pitched on middle, it spins away a bit and makes Bairstow reach. He fetches it and drags his pull shot towards short mid-wicket. His bottom hand comes off the handle and the ball hits the lower half of the bat before flying to Kane who flies to his right to take a screamer. Picture this - he flew to his left on Thursday and does so to his right on a Monday! Pity, we have just two directions, else you could have had seven sides for a week for the Kiwi Kane. Jonny has not made the most of his two lives. A wicket from a nothing ball for the Kiwis and they are all smiles.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Loud shout but the umpire stays put. Wrong one from Todd. He pitches his around off, the ball spins into him and hits the pad of Bairstow, who strides forward in defense. The players appeal to no avail. The New Zealand players think of the review but decide against it. On seeing the Hot Spot, we see that there was a thin inside edge before it hit the pad.
Short ball, Jonny punches this to the off side.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Bouncer! Bairstow ducks under it.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Short on leg, Stokes pulls this with control towards square leg for one.
Similar length, Stokes gets behind the ball and pushes it towards mid off.
Back of a length ball, Stokes covers his stumps and blocks it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Darts this on off, Bairstow punches this along the turf to the off side.
FOUR! Well in control this time. Tossed up this time, in line of the stumps, Bairstow pushes this through mid off for a good-looking boundary.
Straying down leg, Jonny ignores it.

DROPPED! How has Boult put this one down? As easy as it gets. Jonny gets another life. This time on 21. A nothing ball, short and around off, Bairstow tries to pull this but can't connect well enough. The ball flies straight to Boult at mid on who cannot hold onto an easy catch.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Not quite got his line correct from over the wicket, digs this short way down the leg.
Bangs this short too, Stokes gets under it and lets the ball go through.
Stokes gets on his toes to defend this ball.
Short and once again down the leg, Stokes stands tall and evades the bouncer.
Some chin music for the batsman, he lets that bouncer through to the wicket-keeper.
Digs it in short down the leg, easy duck for Ben.
Bairstow has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Short and too wide, Bairstow rocks back and slaps it through covers for a boundary.
Full on leg, Bairstow works it in the gap through square leg for a brace. The trail is now below 200.
Darts this a bit quicker and a tad shorter, Jonny makes room and mistimes his cut.
Serves this around off, Stokes clips it away towards square leg for a single.
Starts off by bowling a flat one outside off, not much turn there and Ben plays this towards covers.
Todd Astle is finally introduced into the attack.
Bairstow chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Bairstow pushes this ball towards mid off for a dot.
Short again, Bairstow gets down on one knee and sways away from it.
Back of a length ball, Jonny blocks it off his back foot.
Bangs this one short, Bairstow does well to leave it.
Runs after 34 balls! Back of a length ball around off, Jonny makes room and punches it off his back foot through covers for a couple of runs.
Wide outside off, easy leave for Ben.
Length around off, Ben walks across and taps the ball in front of him.
Stokes lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Pitches this up further a bit, in line of the stumps, Stokes takes a step and digs out the yorker.
Length ball outside off, too wide to make Stokes play at it.
Bowls this from round the wicket on a good length outside off, Stokes leaves it alone.

Drinks! Although New Zealand picked up Dawid Malan early, Ben Stokes and Jonny Bairstow have done well since then to not give away their wickets. The job is not even half done at this stage, though, as they still trail by 203. The New Zealand bowlers have gone about with their task well yet have just a wicket to show till this interval. Will Todd Astle be the change they want to see?
Another one on a back of a length, Jonny watches it closely and lets it go by getting down on a knee. This is the fourth consecutive maiden.
Back of a length on the stumps, Jonny sways away from the line. The ball thuds into the keeper's gloves.
Pitched up again, Bairstow mistimes his drive towards mid off.
Full length this time, well outside off. Left alone.
Banged short on the stumps, Bairstow crouches low to let it go.
This is angled away and well outside off. Too wide to make Bairstow play.
This length ball is kept out with a defensive shot. Another no-run over, the consecutive dot ball count against the Kiwi all-rounder stands at 28.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, left alone.
This delivery is driven towards covers. 25th ball for no run on the go for Colin.
Fuller on off, defended off the front foot to the off side.
23rd dot ball on the trot against de Grandhomme. He bowls it outside off, Stokes lets it go to the keeper.
The on air commentators are talking about Todd Astle. On this fifth day track, they reckon that the wristspinner could do well and pick up a few wickets and hence want him into the attack soon.
This ball is driven towards covers off the front foot.
Outside off, left alone again. Not making Bairstow play, is Wagner.
Well outside off again, Bairstow points his bat skywards to let it pass.
Harmless delivery outside off, Jonny lets his counterpart do the rest.
This one is punched off the back foot towards covers.
On a length around off, defended off the back foot.
Full and going away from Stokes, he doesn't play at that. Third consecutive maiden for de Grandhomme.
Stokes comes down the track, only to block it with a straight bat.
Hurled outside off, left alone by Ben.
This one is well wide to make Ben play.
Harmless ball outside off, left alone.
On a length around off, punched to the off side for nothing.
This is outside off, left alone.
Full outside off, driven towards covers.
Full outside off, Bairstow looks to drive it through the off side but gets it off the inner half down the ground.
Another one well outside off, left alone.

Good running. Runs after 20 dots. Bairstow works it away towards square leg and sets off for a run. Seeing the keeper go for the ball, the batters decide to take him on and go for the second. Watling has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. A couple results.
Outside off, JB doesn't need to play at those and lets it be.
A small chat between Southee, Williamson and Wagner. Perhaps NZ want to get this done quickly and hence are on the lookout for wickets. A cover as well as a short extra cover in place.
Again Colin gets back to his wide-of-off-stump line, Stokes lets it be. A maiden over, third consecutive one.

Jaffa! This is what de Grandhomme needs to bowl more often. Lands it on a length around middle and leg, Stokes looks to defend it on the initial angle. But the ball nibbles away just a touch and just misses kissing the outside edge.
Yet again. Full, but too wide to make Stokes play.
Same line and length, same action from Ben.
Going away from the batsman on a fuller length, Stokes lets the ball go into the keeper's gloves.
Around off, pushed defensively towards covers.
Outside off on a fuller length, left alone by JB. A maiden to begin for Wagner.
Full again, driven nicely off the front foot towards wide mid off for nothing.

Good shot and an even better effort at covers. This is full outside off, Bairstow drives it crisply towards covers. Seems that a boundary is written all over it but the man at covers dives to his right and parries it towards mid off and it is a dot.
Slanting away from Bairstow on a length, he gets a small stride out and shoulders arms.
Very full outside off, doesn't evoke a stroke from the English wicketkeeper.
Starts with a full ball across Bairstow from over the wicket, Jonny lets it pass to the keeper.
Neil Wagner to bowl for the first time on Day 5. Short-ball tactics?

4 deliveries in this over weren't needed to be played by the batter. De Grandhomme needs to make the batter play at more deliveries if he wants a wicket here. This is again well outside off, Stokes shoulders arms.
Straighter in line, kept out towards mid-wicket.
This one is even wider, Ben lets it pass without playing at it.
Another one in the same area, BS doesn't need to play at those.
Hurled outside off, left alone.
A gentle-paced delivery around middle and off. Stokes looks to defend it off the back foot. Gets a thick edge towards gully.
Dragging his length this time, Stokes cuts it towards backward point and goes to the other end for one. The trail now is 5 more than 200.
This is around off and middle, Ben hangs back and presents a straight defensive bat.
Full on off, defended off the front foot.
Outside off, left alone.
On the pads, Bairstow fails to flick it away. It goes off the pads to the on side and a leg bye is taken.
Hurled on a length outside off, Stokes goes back and punches it through covers. The fielder from mid off hares after it and slides to save a run for the side.
Outside off again, left alone.
This is outside off, Jonny covers his stumps and lets it be.
Overpitched outside off, driven straight to the man at covers.
Full outside off, left alone.
This time, Bairstow gets it past the man there and collects a brace.
Full outside off, driven straight to covers.
Colin de Grandhomme is brought into the attack for the first time today.
Jonny gets this one off the outer half through point for one.
Edged but safe! Bairstow gets an outside edge to this one but the ball lands well in front of Latham at second slip. Lucky Jonny!
FOUR! Nicely stroked. Full on middle and leg, Bairstow pushes it down the ground. The timing is good enough to take it past mid on and to the fence.

DROPPED AND FOUR! Not an easy catch but you expect keepers to take these. This full on the pads, Bairstow looks to flick it and collect some runs. That he does but he should consider himself to be fortunate. He gets a tickle and the ball flies to the left of the keeper. Watling dives to his left and gets a good amount of glove to that yet fails to pouch it. The ball races away to the fine leg fence. In the South Africa-Australia Test, Markram was dropped on 0 and went on to make 84. Can Bairstow repeat or better that?
Fuller on middle and leg, Bairstow pushes it cautiously towards mid on.
Short in length, Ben plays a cross-batted shot towards wide mid on for a single.
Back over the wicket, this one is angled away. Bairstow minds his own business and doesn't bother playing at that.
Banged short on the stumps, JB ducks.
Trent comes round the wicket and bowls it full outside off. Bairstow gets a stride forward and drives it to mid off.
Length ball on the stumps, Jonny blocks it off the back foot.
On the pads, flicked away towards square leg.
Lovely, balanced flick. Full and angling in on middle and leg, Stokes flicks it away through mid-wicket and gets one less than a boundary.

A bit fuller this time, Bairstow is hesitant to get on the front foot. Perhaps his first innings' dismissal has something to do with this. He looks to keep it out from the crease and gets an inside edge onto the front pad.
Length delivery on off, Bairstow goes on the back foot and defends.
Slower one on a length, Stokes is a bit early into the pull. Controls it well and plays it all along the ground in front of square on the leg side for one.
Another delivery slanting away from the southpaw, Stokes covers his stumps and lets it go.
Full and outside off, Stokes lets it go.
Delivered on a length in line of the stumps, Ben blocks it off the back foot.
Again! Indecision from Bairstow, whether to play it or let it be. Gets it off the bottom of the blade to the off side for nothing.
Half-mind. This is slanting away from the right-handed batter. Bairstow isn't sure whether to play it or leave it. Ends up being late in withdrawing his bat and gets it towards the slip cordon.
Shorter in length, pulled away through backward square leg for a single.
Fuller this time, driven towards wide mid off for nothing.
Another length ball, defended off the back foot.
On a length on off, kept out off the back foot.
Kane Williamson has a chat with his bowler and then has an interesting field. There's a leg slip in place, to go with two slips and a gully. Also, a silly mid on stands in attention.
On a length around off, Bairstow shows the full bat face in defending that. A wicket-maiden for Southee.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Bairstow stays on the back foot to this one and pushes it to the off side.
Straight and full outside off, Jonny lets it be.

Jonny Bairstow walks out to bat, replacing Malan. He was in pretty good touch in the ODIs and England would want him to replicate his white-ball form here. Incidentally, it was a wicketkeeper who saved England 5 years ago at the same venue. Is it time for an encore?

OUT! Southee draws the first blood of the day. It's the 'stuck' Malan who is departing. Yes, stuck. He was stuck on the back foot this morning and hardly came forward. Perhaps he needs to get his feet moving somehow to avoid such a dismissal again. This is pitched up on a fuller length and going across Malan. He stays on the back foot and hangs his bat out at that. That's enough this time for the ball to take the edge and fly to the slip cordon. Latham from second slip takes a good catch to his right. Even in the first innings, Malan walked back due to hanging on the back foot and poking. The tourists are still 227 runs behind.
Length ball angling away, Malan lets it be.
This delivery is pushed back towards the bowler. A maiden for Boult now.
Back of a length ball outside off, BS sways away from the line and lets the keeper do the rest.
Full length ball around off, Ben lunges and dead-bats it.
Full and well outside off, Stokes shoulders arms.
On a length around off, Stokes goes back and pushes it tamely towards mid on.
Stokes defends this one watchfully off the front foot.
There's some hammering done near the bowler's run up. Perhaps at the point where Boult takes a leap, there is some unevenness and hence, it was hammered.
This is well outside off, DM lets it be.
Malan drives this one off the front foot towards mid on.
Full on the stumps, flicked towards mid on.

FOUR! Almost works! In the couple of deliveries before this one, Southee pushed Malan on the back foot with his length. After that he pushes this on a fuller length. Malan is yet again hanging on the back foot as he has a feel for this. The ball takes the outside edge but goes through the gap between the slip cordon and gully and goes away to the fence.
Pushes Malan back with this one. Dawid presents a straight bat face to keep it out.
Length ball around off, blocked off the back foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
This is around off and middle, hit to the man at short mid-wicket.
Stokes goes back to this one and defends it.
Change in field. Third slip moves to a catching cover. Wait, now he moves to a short mid-wicket position.
Just away! This is full around off, Stokes drives it back aerially. It goes just past Boult's right and past mid off. A couple taken to get Ben underway.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
In line of the stumps, Stokes gets behind that and pushes it towards mid on.
Another one outside off, left alone. Maiden to begin for Southee.
Full and outside off, left alone by Dawid.
This delivery is driven towards mid off for nothing.
Well done, Tim! This is pitched up right to the batter, Malan just times his push down the ground well. Southee dives to his right in his followthrough and prevents a run.
This one is on the pads, flicked away to square leg for nothing.
Lovely! Southee begins with a beaut of a delivery. Bowls it full and angling away from Malan. The southpaw has to play at it and just has a feel. He is lucky that the ball flew past the outside edge.
Tim Southee will steam in from the other end. Malan will face him.

FOUR! Runs straightaway! Boult steams in and lands it on a length, slanting into Stokes from around off and middle. Ben hops and looks to tuck it away to the on side but gets beaten for pace. The ball goes off the gloves past the diving Watling and through to the fine leg fence. Positive start for the visitors.

It's time for the action on the field to take precedence. Owing to Root's dismissal on what turned out to be the last ball of the day, Ben Stokes makes his way into the middle. He will face Trent Boult, who will run in to deliver a ball that'll complete the over. Dawid Malan waits at the other end. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Mark Richardson doesn't see the need to talk about the weather as it is pretty much clear. He states that the first session was when more swing was seen yesterday. But the ball is not new enough for to see those movement, he adds quickly. He observes some rough patches and footmarks and reckons that Todd Astle will have a major part to play on this last day.

As much as the English fans would love to answer those questions with a 'yes', the Kiwis would do every bit to go 1-0 to the next game. Their bowling has certainly been incisive. After making the visitors toil on the field for more than 3 days, they have been bowling well and THAT Joe Root wicket last evening just seems to have made their task easier. Will they end up being victorious? A mention of the weather is a must in this part of the world and we don't see any hindrances from that aspect. Would this game be done in a trice or do we have a fightback somewhere? Let's see.

For the tourists, a glance at a scorecard of a game that was played on the exact dates as this one five years ago at the very same place may prove to be inspiring. England then salvaged a draw after starting the day at 90/4, chasing 481. A certain Matt Prior played the rescue act then, with some useful support from the others. Who will be their Prior today? Shall we render hopes of an unlikely draw?

7 wickets, 237 runs - we have these figures to start the day. This Test match enters the last day, courtesy rain, that washed away most of Days 2 and 3. Looking at the figures in front of us, it surely is going to be a humongous task for the visitors at hand. Plenty to cheer for the hosts, thus. Welcome to our coverage of Day 5 of the first New Zealand versus England Test, played at Eden Park in Auckland.
... Last Day, First Session ...

Dawid Malan then stepped in and with his skipper he was on the verge to see off the day but Trent Boult put all those thoughts to rest. Right then, England are trailing by 237 runs and need something spectacular to force a draw as they have to face the battle for survival. They do bat deep but the question is will the batsmen to follow next put their hands up or will the Kiwi bowlers just run through the line-up? The weather forecast looks to be really good for Day 5. Join us at 1330 local time (0030 GMT). You can now catch some action from the South Africa vs Australia 3rd Test and World Cup Qualifier final by switching tabs. Until next time, goodbye and cheers!

Henry Nicholl's century and his few useful stands with the lower order earlier in the day powered New Zealand to a massive lead of 369 runs. England were asked to bat but they didn't get an ideal start as Alastair Cook departed cheaply. The pressure was on the visitors and with a full final session remaining in the day, England needed an inspiring partnership. Mark Stoneman and Joe Root joined forces and did exceedingly well to keep the hosts at bay. Neil Wagner, the one who didn't get to bowl in the first innings came out with the short-ball ploy and it worked wonders as he removed the opener as soon as he reached to his fifty.

Off walks Root and that's also to end of a long, long day of Test cricket. All of England would be utterly disappointed with what happened on the last ball of the day. The man who was in for a fight, who was in to show his grit has been sent packing by Trent Boult. The left-arm pacer bowled a deadly spell to dismantle the English skipper and with that dragged the session in his side's favor.

OUT! Oh boy! Root has to depart and is furious about it. The short-ball ploy has done the trick once again for the hosts. Just a ball before he was hit on his fingers which made Trent dig one more in. He bangs this one short too on middle and leg, cramps Root as he couldn't get out of the way. The English skipper tries leaving that one alone but the ball brushes the lower part of the gloves and goes to Watling who leaps to his left and takes a very good catch. The players go up in an appeal and the umpire nods his head. What a bad time for the skipper to lose his wicket. Talks regarding Root and his inability to convert a half century will be continued. More than the conversion, tonight it was just a matter of a ball or so to see off England safely to Stumps. Joe fails to do that which leaves his side in a shaky position.
Good news, folks! Root has put his gloves back on and is ready to face. New Zealand will be looking to attack him with short stuff....
Not looking good for England. The physio comes rushing out with the magic spray. He applies on Root's fingers but this isn't working. Now they apply ice to it. Joe is in agony.

Ouch! That's nasty! Back of a length ball, Root hangs back and looks to block this. The ball rises up after pitching and hits Root on his fingers. That must have hurt him as he is swirling his hand in pain.
Outside off, Root leaves this one alone.
Slightly fuller, Root blocks his stumps and plays it with a straight bat.
Outside off, pitched up, Root has driven it straight down the ground.
Effort ball once again from Wagner, another duck from Malan to evade this.
Back of a length ball, Root pushes this on the off and moves to the other end.
Bangs this one short too on leg, Root ducks at the last moment to let the keeper take it.
Digs this one short too, Dawid pulls it fine down the leg and will get one for it.
Short again, Malan does well to get under this.
Bouncer! Malan ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Neil Wagner comes back to bowl.
Full on leg, Root hits this towards mid on.
Joe now tries flicking a ball that is down the leg side.
The ball is way wide on the leg side but Root still goes after it.
That's fifty for Rooooot...Length outside off, Joe cuts this past point and comes back for the second.
Served around off, Malan steps ahead and pushes this through covers for a single.
Length on off, Malan stands tall and blocks it.

Much better from Malan, but even this cannot find the rope. Hurls this full outside off, Malan gets forward and drives it in the gap through covers. A good effort on the field saves a run for his team.
Malan shoulders arms to let that one through.
Dawid has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Nice shot but doesn't get the timing on it. This is pitched up outside off, Tim drives it through covers for a couple of runs.
Outside off on a good length, Dawid goes for the poke but gets beaten.
Full in line of the stumps, Malan covers his stumps and hits it back to the bowler.
Defended off the back foot by Root.
Length on off, Root leans forward and plays it with soft hands.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Sudden bounce on that. Boult serves this at a back of a length, it takes a sudden bounce after pitching and hits Joe on his gloves. No damage done.
Length in line of the stumps, Root is solid in his defense.
Lands this full outside off, Root drives this to the mid off region.
Length on off, Dawid pushes this for the covers fielder to pick up.
Back of a length ball, Malan covers his stumps and plays it towards mid off.
On off, Malan stays in his crease and blocks it.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Malan pulls this with authority and dispatches it from his sight. Tim bowls this short and Malan pulls it front of square on the leg side for a boundary.
Steams in from over the wicket and serves it at a back of a length ball on off. Malan hangs back and taps it in front of him.
Root defends it from within the crease on the off side.
Pitched up around off, Root takes a step forward and drives it to mid on.
Digs this in short, Root ducks under it.
Late movement for Boult. Serves this outside off, Root goes for the poke but the ball keeps low and moves away from him as he misses his shot.
Outside off, Root opens the face of the bat and guides it towards backward point.
Comes in from over the wicket and lands this just around off. Root plays it with soft hands into the ground.
Full outside off, easy leave for Dawid.
Outside off, Malan leaves this alone.
Dawid has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Pitched up, Dawid drives it for the cover fielder to collect.
Length around off, Malan drives it towards mid off.
Back of a length ball, Malan tucks it away for a dot.
Back of a length ball, Root stands tall and plays it with a straight back.
Pitches this up again, Root gets low and drives it through covers for a brace.
Root defends it from within the crease.
Back of a length ball, Malan goes for the tuck and gets hit on the thigh pad. They take a run as the ball rolls towards square leg.
Back of a length ball, Malan hops and plays it on the ground.
Length on middle, Malan hits it back to the bowler.
Drags his length back now, Root does well to evade it.
FOUR! Excellent straight drive. Overpitched ball on middle and off, Root gets forward and drives it through mid off for a boundary.
Bouncer! Root ducks in time to let that one go over him.
On that off stump channel, Root sees the ball go through to the keeper.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Length outside off, Root points his bat skywards and leaves it alone.
Pitched up, Root punches this to covers and quickly moves to the other end.
In line of the stumps, Root shows Boult the sticker of his bat.
Full, around off, Root leans ahead and drives it with confidence towards covers.
Length outside off, Root gets forward and drives it to mid off for a dot.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Length on middle, Root plays this towards mid on.
Full on leg, Malan flicks it in the gap through square leg for a couple of runs.
Outside off, Malan chooses to leave this alone.
Around off, Malan tries slicing this to point but gets beaten.
Malan defends it from within the crease.
Strays down the leg, Malan goes after it and misses his flick.
Length on off, swings away after pitching, Malan fails to put bat on ball.
Length around off, Root cuts it to point.
Pitched up on middle, Root drives this through covers for a brace.
Length on middle, Malan pushes this towards mid-wicket and quickly scampers to the other end.
Dawid has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Malan lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Full and wide outside off, easy leave for Malan.
Outside off, Root shoulders arms to this one.
Digs this in short, Root sways away from this one.
Angles this away from Malan who works it down the leg for one.
Length on middle and leg, Dawid plays it with a straight bat.
Strays down the pads of Root who clips it away towards square leg and picks up a single.
Comes in from over the wicket and lands it around off, Root covers his stumps and taps it in front of him.
Length on off, solid defense from Dawid.
Malan has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Leaves this ball outside his off pole.
FOUR! Cut and cut well. Wide outside off, Malan opens his arms and gets it in the gap through backward point for a boundary.
Outside off, easy leave for Dawid.
Outside off, easy leave for Malan.
Pitched up on off, Joe pushes this to mid off and shouts 'Noooo...' to his partner.
Back of a length ball on off, Root hangs back and taps it in front of him.
On the fourth stump line, Root watches the ball go to the keeper.
Serves one up for a change, Root drives it to mid off for nothing.
Bangs this short, Root gets low and allows the ball to pass by.
Joe shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Peach! Lands this on middle and off, the ball moves away after pitching and almost gets the outside edge of Malan's bat.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Root has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Classical Root. Pitched up ball on middle, Root stands tall and pushes it down the ground for a boundary.
Length outside off, Root shoulders arms to it.
Ends with another bouncer, Dawid evades this one too.
Short again, Malan ducks under it.
Meanwhile, Dawid Malan walks in next to bat.
Drinks have been called. England were going well until Stoneman fell into the trap.

OUT! The short-ball ploy has worked for New Zealand and Wagner is all pumped up. After three back-to-back short balls, Wagner continues to dig it in but this time he changes the angle and comes from around the wicket. Stoneman looks to pull but gets a top edge instead. The ball though, does not travel far enough and goes towards the deep square leg region. Trent Boult comes rushing in from fine leg and takes a very good catch diving forward. The 88-run partnership is broken. Is this the opening for the hosts?

SIX! Top edge and it goes sailing over the fence! That's fifty for Mark Stoneman! Wagner bangs this short again and the southpaw goes for the pull again. He gets a top edge to it and the ball flies over the fine leg region for a biggie. It's been a good knock from the English opener so far.
FOUR! Gets this fine and it will race away to the fence. Short again, Mark pulls towards the fine leg region for a single.
Short ball on middle, Stoneman pulls this in the gap through mid-wicket and does well to come for the second.
Defended off the back foot by Root.
Mark drives this through covers and they pick up a run.
Wide outside off, Stone goes for the cut but doesn't connect it well. Gets an bottom edge to it and the ball goes towards gully.
Short ball, Mark goes for the pull but misses it.
Full in line of the stumps, Stoneman plays this with a straight bat.
Bouncer! Stoneman does well to evade it.
Wagner digs in a short one on middle, Joe Root ducks under it.
Short delivery on middle and leg,  Stoneman helps it down with a pull towards fine leg for a single.
Gets back and tucks it through square leg for a single.
Back of a length delivery outside off, punched in front of extra cover for a single.

Really good effort from Colin de Grandhomme! Short ball, slanting away, Root hops back and punches it square on the off side. The ball races away and de Grandhomme gives it a chase. Does really well to pull the ball back in play. Saves a run for his side.
Angling away from off, Root points his bat skywards and makes a leave.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Another leading edge. Stoneman once again tries to flick it away but is early into the shot. Gets it off the leading edge which falls short of the man at extra cover.
Fuller in length on the stumps, Stoneman looks to flick but gets a soft leading edge.
Good length ball outside off, pushed through cover for a single.
Covers the line and defends well.
Straying on the pads, flicked behind square on the leg side for a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Short of a length ball on middle, Stoneman hops back and tucks it past the the vacant short leg region for a single. There was a shy made at the bowler's end but Stoneman was well in.
Bangs in a short one on middle, Stoneman ducks.
Another one on a shorter length on middle, tucked towards mid on for a single.
Replica of the previous delivery.
Digs in a short ball on middle, Root ducks.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Beaten! Lures Stoneman forward to play at it but the ball moves away and beats him.
Length delivery on the stumps, knocked back to the bowler.
Driven towards the fielder at mid off.
Shortish outside off, Stoneman looks to cut but gets a bottom edge towards point.
Good length delivery on middle and off, punched back to the bowler.
Make it four in a row! Angling away once again, nothing doing says Joe.
That's third leave in a row! Seams away from a fuller length, the English skipper pays no heed.
Fuller ball outside off, Joe Root is happy to make a leave.
Pitched up delivery on off, left alone.
Shortish on middle and off, stabbed out towards cover.
Back of a length delivery outside off, punched towards the left of the bowler.
Colin keeps it full on the stumps, bunted back to the bowler.
Another leave from the southpaw.
Doesn't go after it this time as he makes a good leave.
Shortish ball, angling away on off, Mark Stoneman without any feet movement looks to go hard at it with a cut shot. Is beaten all ends up.
FOUR! Jeet Raval, that's really sloppy brother! Fuller ball on the stumps, Stoneman drives it towards mid on. The New Zealand opener lets it through his legs and concedes a boundary.
On a length outside off, punched off the back foot towards cover.
Good length delivery on the stumps, water-tight defense from Joe Root to end the first over of Wagner.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

The crowd Booooooos! Wagner comes steaming in and just when he was about to deliver, Root pulls out as something distracted him. He smiles and apologizes but tell you what, it's something that a fast bowler would never be pleased with. Poor Wagner will have to walk back...
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball - but fails.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They manage to come back for the second.
Is right behind the line to this length ball and defends it down.
Comes running in from over the wicket and lands it on a fuller length on the pads, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
Finally, Neil Wagner to have a go. First time in this Test.
Length ball outside off, steered with an angled bat towards the gully  fielder.
Angling away on a length outside off, easily left alone by Stoneman. He has shown good patience till now, good for England.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On the pads, eased fine down the leg side for a single.
Fullish in length and angling in on middle, worked away towards mid on.
On a good length outside off, punched past the cover fielder for a single.
On middle and off, Joe Root stays right behind the line and defends it down.
Fullish ball on the pads, worked away towards the mid-wicket fielder.

Good stop! Saved a certain boundary there! Short and outside off, width given as well. Stoneman stands tall and cuts it hard towards point where the fielder dives to his right to cut it off. He saves three runs for his side.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Angles it away on a fuller length outside off, easily left alone.
Southee in his bid to attack the stumps ends up straying on the pads, glanced down to fine leg for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
Veering on the pads, clipped through mid-wicket for a comfortable brace.

Huge shout for an LBW, not given! De Grandhomme angles it in from around off, Root looks to flick it away but seems to have gotten an inside edge on the pads as the ball rolls behind square on the leg side and they run one. New Zealand appeal but the umpire turns it down as he spots an inside edge. Good call.
Back of a length delivery outside off, steered down to third man for a double.
Pitched up ball outside off, driven towards mid off.
Fullish in length outside off, JR is happy to leave it alone.
Colin de Grandhomme is back into the attack. The on-air commentators want Kane to bring Neil Wagner on. His pace will surely trouble the batters, they feel.
On middle, clipped towards the fielder at mid-wicket for nothing.
Stoneman eases this full ball straight to mid off.
50-run stand comes up between the two. Some relief in the English camp. Fuller ball on the pads, flicked towards mid-wicket for a single.
Fullish delivery on middle and off, Root drives it straight to mid on.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On middle and off, defended off the back foot.
Mark chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
The stand moves to 49 now! Short of a length delivery, in the channel outside off, Stoneman tries to punch but gets it off the outer half behind point for an easy brace.
Delivers it on a fuller length outside off, pushed towards the man at mid off.
Back of a length delivery on middle, skidding a bit off the deck, MS misses his tuck and wears it on the thigh pad.

FOUR! Easy peasy for the southpaw! Boult sprays it on the pads, all Mark had to do was to get some bat on it. He shuffles across and does so. Next result - the ball crosses the fine leg fence. 50 comes up for England.
Martin Guptill is on the field as a substitute. A bit of a delay as there is some movement behind the bowler...
Drops it on a back of a length, angling in on middle, tapped in front of point.
Covers the sticks, is right behind the line and defends it down watchfully.
Very full outside off, Stoneman looks to drive but once again mistimes it towards mid off. The man is a bit deep there which allows them to steal a single.
Fullish in length and curling back in on the pads, a mistimed flick towards mid-wicket.
Good length delivery outside off, punched towards cover for nothing.
Good tempting line from Southee! Fullish on off, Mark shows good resistance as he lets it be.
Slanting away on a fuller length outside off, shouldered arms to.
On middle and leg, worked with soft hands towards mid-wicket.
Bangs in a short one on middle and off, Root arches back to evade it.
FOUR! Similar from Root this time! Boult angles it away on a length outside off, Root reaches out to that one as he deftly guides it behind point and picks up a boundary to his name.
Nicely done! Short of a length delivery outside off, Stoneman stands tall and steers it through point. Won't get a boundary but will pick up three.

A shout for an LBW but it was going down leg. Good length delivery, angling in on middle and leg, Stoneman misses his tuck and wears it on the pads. Boult slips in his followthrough and is down on the ground. Still appeals for it but it was going down leg.
Takes a stride ahead to a fuller ball and eases it into the cover region for a single.
Good length delivery, just around off, Mark hangs back to defend but the ball catches the outside edge and goes on the bounce to Watling behind. The key there was he played with soft hands.
Southee pitches it up but no swing on this one, Stoneman pats it towards mid off.
Fuller ball, coming back in on the pads, Stoneman flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Angling away on a fuller length outside off, left alone with ease.
Very full outside off, Mark squeezes it out in front of the point fielder.
Fuller in length from over the wicket, Stoneman points his bat skywards as he makes an assured leave.
Tim Southee will bowl from the other end.

That stayed low! Boult and Root share a smile. Ahead of a length outside off, Root crouches low to defend but the ball sneaks under his bat and rolls on the bounce to the keeper behind. A maiden for Trent to kick things off in this session.
Good length delivery on middle, curling back in a wee bit, Root stabs it out comfortably.
Goes fuller, angling away on off, Joe Root plants his front foot across as he makes another leave.
Drags his length a tad, JR covers the line and shows a straight bat.
Slightly fuller on off, Joe Root leans forward a touch and defends it down solidly.
He comes from over the wicket and hurls it across on off, Root is happy to shoulder his arms.
The players are making their way out in the middle for the final session. The batsmen have taken their guards. Trent Boult will bowl the first over post dinner. Three slips and a gully in place...
... Day 4, Session 3 ...

It is going to be an interesting last session now for the three lions. They will be batting under lights and the ball is still new. Joe Root and Mark Stoneman have looked tentative till now and need to find a way to counter it out there. New Zealand, well their bowlers are relatively fresh and would be licking their lips to go in now. This promises to be an exciting session with the ball moving around. Do join us for that in a short while as this can decide the outcome of this Test match.

No further alarms for England after the early loss of Alastair Cook. Root and Stoneman ensure that England can have a better supper for now but they are still way behind in the Test match. Early on, the New Zealand tail wagged along with Henry Nicholls which helped them propel their lead to 369 before declaring the innings. England had their backs against the wall and to make matters worse, they lost Cook in this brief passage of play which further dented them.
Wide outside off stump, Stoneman leaves it alone. That's Dinner, England trail by 331!
FOUR! Beautifully done! Another pitched up ball on middle and leg, Stoneman hits it along the turf through mid on for a boundary.
Pitched up, Mark hits it to mid on.
Back of a length ball on leg, Mark his hit high on the thigh pad after missing his flick.

FOUR. Digs this in short on middle and off, Stoneman pulls this away through mid-wicket. Jeet Raval the fielder there, dives and stops the ball but after the umpire confirming it with the TV umpire, it seems that Raval has touched the rope when he had the ball in his hands.
Comes in from over the wicket, lands it on a good length around off and it moves away from Stoneman after pitching who is happy to let it be.
Length around off, Root plays it into the ground with soft hands.
Covers his stumps and taps it in front of him.
FOUR. Full outside off, Root leans forward and slices it uppishly just past the third slip fielder. The ball runs away to the fence for a boundary.
Pitched up, Stoneman drives it towards covers and quickly pushes for the run.
Outside off, Stoneman doesn't bother fiddling with it.
A tad fuller, on middle and off, Mark plays it to cover-point.
Root has flicked the ball off his pads.
Back of a length ball on off, Mark punches this through the line for a single.
Beauty! Almost got the outside edge of Stoneman's bat. Lands this on middle at a good length, invites Mark forward who gets beaten on his defense.
This ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for Stoneman.
Mark shoulders arms to let that one through.
Outside off, Stoneman chooses to leave it alone.
Played through mid-wicket by Joe.
Boult is playing with the angle, comes steaming in from over the wicket now. Pitches it on middle and leg, Root is solid in his defense.
Comes from round the wicket, lands it at a back of a length, Root hangs back and slices it to the point fielder.
On that fourth stump line, Root watches it go through the keeper.
Outside off, left alone.
Joe chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Outside off, Stoneman fails to put bat on ball.
Wide outside off stump, Mark leaves it alone.
Will get just one this time as he flicks it towards square the leg fielder.
Finds the gap this time, Root flicks it in the gap through mid-wicket for a brace.
Pushes his length further up, Joe works it to square leg.
Root rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball on the off.
Around off, Stoneman punches this through cover-point. Finds the gap and after some confusion they still manage to get the second.
Short outside off, Stoneman goes for the upper cut but arches back a way too much. He gets beaten and the keeper collects it at a good height.
This one will be picked up by the mid on fielder after Stoneman hits it to him.
Pitches it up on leg, Mark flicks this for the square leg fielder to collect.
Back of a length ball, Stoneman hangs back and blocks it.
FOUR BYES! Over Stoneman and Watling and runs away to the fine leg boundary. Boult bangs this one short, Stoneman ducks under it and it goes over the keeper for a boundary.
Covers his stumps and taps it in front of him.
This ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for Joe.
Hint of swing from Southee. Serves this on off, the ball moves away from Root who looks to flirt at it but gets beaten.
Full on middle and off, Stoneman slices this towards covers for a run.
Fuller in length just outside off, Stoneman gets low and looks to drive but is beaten once again.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
On that fourth stump channel, Root plants his foot forward, but gets beaten outside his off pole.
Root shoulders arms to let that one through.
Peach! Very good line and length from Boult. Lands this around off, the ball jags back and goes through the gap between bat and pad. Almost gets an inside edge to the keeper.
Full around off, Joe drives this for the mid off fielder to collect.
Root lets the ball go outside his off stump.
The ball is too wide on the off side for Root to make any contact.
Superb drive through covers. Full outside off, Root leans ahead and drives it in the gap and will come back for the third run.
Root covers his stumps and blocks this.
FOUR! Top edge but safe! Tim bangs this one short on leg, Root goes for the pull but gets a top edge fine down the leg side. A streaky way to get your first boundary.
Root shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Root defends it from within the crease.
Full on off, Stoneman looks to clip it away but is a bit early in closing the face of the bat. Gets a leading edge towards cover for a single.
Ohh! Length down the leg, Root goes after it but misses his flick. A very good over comes to an end.
Joe Root walks to the middle to bat next. A lot of responsibility lies on his shoulders.

OUT! Caught down the leg side! An early wicket and the Chef has to depart. This is what happens when you don't get your feet moving. He was on his back foot for previous length balls but Boult pitches this one full and it is heading down leg. Cook goes for the lazy flick but gets a feather to it. The ball goes towards Watling who dives to his right and takes a good low catch. The players go up in unison and it didn't take time for the umpire to raise his finger. A dejected Cook has to take the long walk back. Back-to-back failures for the southpaw.
Short and wide, Cook cuts it towards gully. Williamson stationed there, dives and manages to get fingertips to it. It took the sting of the ball and the batsmen pick up a couple.
Length ball on the stumps, Cook covers his stump and blocks it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Pitched up, Cook plays this to mid-wicket for nothing.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Up and over. Tim drags his length back, Stoneman rocks back and pulls it over mid-wicket for the first boundary. That should give him some confidence.
Outside off, Stoneman plays at it but gets an edge which lands short of Williamson at gully. The Kiwi skipper dives to stop a certain boundary.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Slower ball on a good length, Stoneman looks to work it on the on side but gets a leading edge well short of the bowler.
Tim lands this from over the wicket outside off, Stoneman doesn't bother playing at it.
Tim Southee will bowl from the other end.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. Boult continuing from where he left off, a maiden to begin with now.
Length around off, Cook shoulders arms to this one.
Outside off, Cook chooses to leave it alone.
This time Cook gets behind the ball and blocks it.
Another play and a miss. Length around the fourth stump channel, Cook plays but gets beaten.
Boult starts with a length delivery just outside off, Cook pokes at it but misses.
